LESSON: WRITING 10.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING: DESCRIPTIVE COMPOSITION (120 -160 WORDS)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Composition (120 -160 words)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Composition (120 -160 words), part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: How do we describe things or events? 2. Why is it important to describe things or events clearly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe people or things mentioned in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Composition (120 -160 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. create a descriptive composition related to the theme for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Composition (120 -160 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. critique a composition on the choice of words, creativity, relevance to theme and logical flow.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Composition (120 -160 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. Appreciate a well written composition from a text Learner is guided to: • Read a sample composition from print or electronic sources. • Talk about people or things in the text. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application or point/sign or write to express their views. • Make sentences to describe how they spent their leisure time collaboratively. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application or point/sign or write their sentences. 1. How do we describe things or events? 2. Why is it important to describe things or events clearly? 91 • Organise the sentences to make a paragraph collaboratively. • Write a descriptive composition individually. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology to type or write. • Proof read the composition with peers.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Composition (120 -160 words) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Respect is fosterd as the learner writes descriptive compositions about various characters.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills Education is nurtured as the learner acquires effective communication skills when organizing and writing

compositions.

Link to other Objects:

The learner can apply descriptive composition writing skills to Kiswahili as they learn the same concept.
